claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're asking about, and if so, how many children are you responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 5 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 5 years old and lives with you at home.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and general upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I take care of all his day-to-day needs, his food, clothes, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living with someone else for any period of time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex lives at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually there's a bit of a situation there. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for him, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about that situation. This is an important detail.

According to the Child Benefit rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. When two people are responsible for the same child and cannot agree who should claim, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will make the decision about who will receive it.

Let me ask: **Is the other parent currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has neither of you claimed yet?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Neither of us has claimed yet. That's why I'm here - I want to claim it, but we haven't been able to agree on who should.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more question to complete my assessment:

**Do you or the other parent have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** (This won't affect your eligibility, but it may mean you'd need to pay a tax charge on the Child Benefit received.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into income details right now - I'm just trying to figure out if I'm actually eligible to claim in the first place, given our situation with not being able to agree.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's completely understandable. I have enough information to assess your eligibility now.

Based on what you've told me, let me provide my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the eligibility requirements:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is under 16 (he's 5 years old)
- You're responsible for his care and provide for his needs
- He lives with you full-time

**Regarding the disagreement with Alex's other parent:** The fact that you can't agree on who should claim does NOT make you ineligible. According to the rules, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child. If both of you apply and cannot agree, HMRC will make the decision about who will receive it.

**What to do next:** You can go ahead and make your claim for Child Benefit. If the other parent also applies, HMRC will help resolve the situation and decide who should receive the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
